accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS RL.4.3 (describe in depth a character, setting or event, drawing on specific details such as thoughts, words or actions) and standard terms: direct and indirect characterisation, trait versus feeling, sensory language and mood. Every story clue was checked by hand: the harbour master and Grandad lines are other characters' responses, the italic-style thought is inside Nell's head, and each part has exactly one clue that fits 'determined'.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips: using looks as evidence of a trait (step 0 prediction, red raincoat chip, pair 4, challenge tag looks), giving one quote from one page (step 1 prediction, tag one), choosing a quote that shows a different trait (laughing at gulls, mastery m8), listing facts instead of sense details (Tuesday and 1890 chips, tag fact), and retelling an event without saying how it changed the character (chain step 'Change').

lab_distinct.evidence: Built around one story, The Lighthouse Key: a 4-box clue sort (says, does, thinks, others respond), a three-part evidence hunt that refuses a second clue from the same part, a setting paragraph whose sense details unlock the mood choice, an event chain filled left to right, and deep-versus-thin description pairs. Gate similarity under 30% to flagcharm, flaginfer and flagsmap.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the method: looks and off-trait clues are refused with a reason, a second clue from the same part is refused until the other parts are covered, mood cannot be chosen until every sense detail is found, and the chain only accepts the next link. The banner after each win states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Their hair and clothes' tell you most, 'one clue proves it', and 'dates and facts about the place' help you picture a setting best.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged distractors and targeted feedback: looks (looks are not character), setting (that is about the place), one (a trait shows across the story), none (a description without evidence is only opinion), sense (name the sense for each detail), fact, thin (naming the place is not enough).

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 2.9 and adult 6.3 (limits 6.5 and 9.5). Trait, setting, mood and sense detail are each defined in plain words; story sentences are short and concrete.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph teaches one thing: what a deep description is, the four kinds of clue, evidence across the story, settings and events. Explanation under 12% similar to lessons 795, 166 and 726.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 and desktop screenshots of every step (/workspace/wn-run-1116-1351/shots/dc-*, dcd-*). Story chips wrap to two lines where needed, the intro line wraps, the four chain boxes become a 2x2 grid on phones with 11 px filled text, and the 2x2 clue boxes and mood buttons stay readable and tappable.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes, no console errors. Every chip, mood, chain card and pair has a matching button, and the canvas aria-label reads the current clue, all story chips, the sense details found, or both descriptions in a pair.
